applies_why: The judge text assigns UNDERDETERMINED to Isaiah 7:14 because the challenger addressed the virgin/young-woman wording while the defender addressed the prophetic application, treating the verse's dual senses as leaving the matter open.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- Challenger answered the virgin and young-woman wording in [DR3] and defender answered the prophetic application in [CR2] and [CR3].
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: The rule phrase 'A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand' could be read as (1) dual senses may not support UNDERDETERMINED, or (2) divergent senses make the question open; I weigh them as the rule plainly forbids treating dual senses as open.
why: The judge made UNDERDETERMINED from the competing virgin/young-woman and prophetic-application senses, but K-S2 says a verse with two senses at once is not open and both senses stand.
